questions.stem: Copper oxide is a base but not an alkali. Sodium hydroxide is both a base and an alkali. What is the key difference?

options.text: Copper oxide is acidic, not basic
Sodium hydroxide dissolves in water to form OH- ions, but copper oxide is insoluble in water
Copper oxide does not react with acids
All metal compounds are alkalis

questions.explanation: A base is any substance that neutralises an acid. An alkali is a special type of base that dissolves in water to produce hydroxide ions (OH-). Sodium hydroxide dissolves in water (NaOH -> Na+ + OH-), making it an alkali. Copper oxide neutralises acids but does not dissolve in water, so it is a base but not an alkali.

questions.stem: A student adds excess copper oxide powder to warm dilute sulfuric acid. The black powder gradually disappears and the solution turns blue. Some black powder remains at the bottom. Why is excess copper oxide used?

options.text: To make the reaction happen faster
To ensure all the acid is neutralised, so the resulting solution is not acidic
To produce more copper sulfate crystals
Copper oxide only reacts when there is excess present

questions.explanation: Using excess copper oxide ensures that all the sulfuric acid is used up (neutralised). The excess unreacted copper oxide can then be filtered off, leaving a pure solution of copper sulfate without any remaining acid. If not enough base were added, the solution would still contain acid, contaminating the salt.

questions.stem: Which of the following substances is an alkali?

options.text: Iron oxide (Fe2O3)
Calcium hydroxide (Ca(OH)2)
Copper carbonate (CuCO3)
Silicon dioxide (SiO2)

questions.explanation: Calcium hydroxide is slightly soluble in water and produces OH- ions when dissolved, making it an alkali. Iron oxide and copper carbonate are bases (they neutralise acids) but are insoluble in water, so they are not alkalis. Silicon dioxide is actually an acidic oxide, not a base.

questions.stem: Indigestion tablets often contain magnesium hydroxide or calcium carbonate. How do these substances relieve indigestion?

options.text: They coat the stomach lining to protect it
They are bases that neutralise excess stomach acid (HCl)
They absorb water from the stomach
They increase acid production to speed up digestion

questions.explanation: Indigestion is caused by excess hydrochloric acid in the stomach. Magnesium hydroxide and calcium carbonate are bases that neutralise the excess acid. For example: Mg(OH)2 + 2HCl -> MgCl2 + 2H2O. This reduces the acidity and relieves the discomfort. This is a practical everyday application of neutralisation.

questions.stem: Alkalis feel soapy to the touch and can be just as corrosive as strong acids. Which ion is responsible for the properties of alkaline solutions?

options.text: H+ ions (hydrogen ions)
Na+ ions (sodium ions)
OH- ions (hydroxide ions)
O2- ions (oxide ions)

questions.explanation: Hydroxide ions (OH-) are responsible for the characteristic properties of alkalis: soapy feel, pH above 7, turning litmus blue, and corrosive nature at high concentrations. Just as H+ ions determine acidic properties, OH- ions determine alkaline properties. All alkalis produce OH- ions in aqueous solution.
